entities.summary: Templar of Tyre is the conventional designation of the anonymous 14th-century historian who compiled the Old French chronicle known as the Deeds of the Cypriots. The Deeds was written between about 1315 and 1320 on Cyprus and presents a history of the Crusader states and the Kingdom of Cyprus from 1132 down to 1309 as well as an account of the trials of the Templars in 1314. It is divisible into three parts and the third, which is the original work of the compiler, is the most important source for the final years of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and one of only two eyewitness accounts of the fall of Acre in 1291.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Templar of Tyre's Deeds of the Cypriots provides a unique eyewitness account of the fall of Acre in 1291 and offers insight into the trials of the Templars in 1314, shedding light on the final years of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
